c.tagline: A laid-back Sinai backpacker town famous for the Blue Hole dive site and cheap beachfront cafes
langs: English (widely spoken due to backpacker/diving tourism)

card: Accepted at larger dive centers and hotels; cash preferred at beachfront cafes and markets

taxi.fareNote: Dahab is small enough to walk or bike between most areas; taxis mainly used for airport transfers or desert excursions

emergency.note: Tourist police (180) can assist with English-language support

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Central Dahab (Masbat and Mashraba) is very walkable along the beachfront promenade; the Blue Hole and Canyon require a short taxi ride

safety.safety: Generally safe and relaxed, popular with solo travelers and long-term digital nomads; check current travel advisories for the wider Sinai region
safety.crime: Very low crime; diving safety (especially at the Blue Hole) is the main practical caution

hood_landmark.Masbat / Asalah: Masbat's beachfront promenade of cafes and dive shops
hood_landmark.Mashraba: Mashraba's central restaurant and shopping strip

avoid.reason: Avoid overland travel into the North and interior Sinai away from the main coastal road, which most governments advise against due to security risks.
Vendor hassle is mild by Egyptian standards, but vet dive and quad-bike operators carefully and refuse any drug offers — penalties are severe.

hood_desc: The bohemian northern beachfront strip of cushion-seated cafes, dive centers, and budget guesthouses, the heart of Dahab's backpacker scene.
The central strip with the highest concentration of restaurants, shops, and mid-range hotels.
A quieter, more residential area to the south, popular for longer stays away from the tourist bustle.

water.note: Tap water is desalinated and brackish; drink bottled water.

transit.sys: No formal municipal transit; walking, bikes, and taxis cover the compact town
transit.map: Not applicable; the town is small and easily walkable
transit.note: Most excursions (Blue Hole, Canyon, Mount Sinai) are arranged through dive centers or hotels

transport.air: Sharm El Sheikh International Airport (SSH), about 1-1.5 hr away, is the nearest major airport
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Dahab
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Cairo, Sharm El Sheikh, and Nuweiba
transport.car: Rental cars available; taxis and shared minibuses are the more common way to arrive from Sharm El Sheikh

airport.name: Sharm El Sheikh International Airport (nearest major gateway)
airport.transport: Taxi, shared minibus, or hotel transfer

net.w: Free wifi standard in cafes and guesthouses
net.ops: Vodafone Egypt, Orange Egypt, Etisalat Misr
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in cafes, popular with digital nomads
net.ap: A Vodafone or Orange Egypt tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10-15% is customary for dive guides and instructors

landmarks: Blue Hole
The world-famous 100-metre submarine sinkhole north of town lures freedivers and snorkellers to its coral-rimmed rim and legendary Arch.
The Lighthouse Reef
Right off Dahab's promenade, this gently shelving house reef delivers superb easy diving and snorkelling amid coral gardens and shoals of reef fish.
Three Pools
A trio of turquoise coral-ringed lagoons south of town near Asalah, offering some of Sinai's most colourful shore snorkelling.
Blue Lagoon
Beyond Ras Abu Galum lies this dreamy shallow bay of impossibly turquoise water, a kitesurfing and camel-trek paradise with rustic Bedouin camps.
Ras Abu Galum Protectorate
A wild protectorate of mountains meeting reef reached by camel or boat, combining pristine dive sites with solar-powered Bedouin settlements.
The Canyon
A dramatic underwater fissure just north of Dahab where divers descend through shafts of sunlight into a narrow coral-encrusted crack.
Eel Garden
A sandy-bottomed bay at Asalah where hundreds of garden eels sway from the seabed like grass, a mesmerising snorkel from shore.
Mount Sinai (Jebel Musa)
A pre-dawn day trip from Dahab climbs Moses' 2,285-metre holy summit for a sunrise revered by three faiths over granite peaks.
Saint Catherine's Monastery
At Sinai's foot stands the world's oldest continuously inhabited Christian monastery, a UNESCO treasury guarding the Burning Bush and ancient icons.
Coloured Canyon
A day trip into the Sinai desert threads this narrow sandstone slot canyon, its swirling walls banded in rose, gold and purple.

train.note: There is no railway anywhere in Sinai. Egyptian National Railways stops west of the Suez Canal, so travel here is entirely by road or by flying into Sharm El Sheikh, about 90 minutes south.

intl.to: Aqaba (Jordan) - via the Nuweiba ferry, ~1 hr by road to the port
intl.op: East Delta Travel bus to Nuweiba — tickets at the Dahab bus station

intl.to: Eilat (Israel) - via the Taba border, ~2 hr
intl.op: East Delta Travel bus to Taba — tickets at the Dahab bus station

bus.note: Both international routes mean a bus to the border or port and a change on the far side rather than a through coach. Taba is about two hours north and the crossing into Eilat is straightforward on foot; Nuweiba is an hour away for the Jordan ferry. Carry your passport and check current Sinai travel advice. Go Bus (https://go-bus.com/) and East Delta run to Cairo in 8-9 hours and Sharm in 90 minutes.

intl.to: Aqaba (Jordan) - sails from Nuweiba, ~1 hr north of Dahab, ~1-3 hr crossing
intl.op: AB Maritime — tickets at the Nuweiba port

ferry.note: There is no ferry from Dahab itself. The Nuweiba-Aqaba crossing an hour up the coast is the only sea route out of Sinai and the practical way into Jordan for Petra - the fast catamaran takes about an hour and the car ferry three, but departures are notoriously loose and can be delayed by hours. Buy the ticket at the port, carry your passport, and expect a Jordanian visa on arrival for most nationalities.

half.name: Nuweiba
half.blurb: Quieter Red Sea coastal town north of Dahab with palm-lined beaches, Bedouin camps, and calmer diving spots.

half.name: Sharm El Sheikh
half.blurb: Larger Red Sea resort town with Naama Bay's promenade, dive centers, and boat trips out to offshore reefs.

full.name: Petra
full.blurb: Ancient Nabataean city carved into rose-colored cliffs, reached by ferry across the Gulf of Aqaba to Jordan.

full.name: Ras Mohammed National Park
full.blurb: Protected headland at the tip of the Sinai Peninsula with sheer reef walls and some of the Red Sea's richest marine life.
